title: Over the fifteen months tested the live settings lose on both symbols
detail: Each quarter was run eight times on raw ticks on a fresh $2,000 with the live unit auto-step, with only the loop's timing drawn at random. Median result per quarter, gold: Aug–Nov 2025 −$2,000; Nov 2025–Feb 2026 −$2,000; Feb–May 2026 −$2,000; May–Aug 2026 −$2,000; Aug–Nov 2026 −$2,000; 40 of 40 quarter-runs lost money and 40 ended with the account stopped out. BTC: Aug–Nov 2025 −$2,000; Nov 2025–Feb 2026 −$2,000; Feb–May 2026 −$112; May–Aug 2026 −$2,000; Aug–Nov 2026 −$47; 37 of 40 lost money and 22 were stopped out. Run as one continuous account from 13 Aug 2025, gold was stopped out on 23 Sep 2025, day 41 and BTC was stopped out on 14 Oct 2025, day 63. On gold every one of the 40 quarter-runs ended with the account stopped out; on BTC the three months you asked for were the least bad of the five.

title: It loses more baskets than it wins, and a few large ladder baskets decide the result
detail: Gold, 13 Aug–13 Nov 2026: 38.4% of 393 baskets won, and it needs 39.5% to break even, because the average win is +$281.14 and the average loss −$183.69 (the average win is larger than the average loss). The worst basket lost $8,064, as much as 29 average wins; the ten worst gave back 54% of everything the winners made. The quarter ended −$2,000. BTC, 13 Aug–13 Nov 2026: 35.4% of 628 baskets won, and it needs 35.7% to break even, because the average win is +$26.51 and the average loss −$14.71 (the average win is larger than the average loss). The worst basket lost $578, as much as 22 average wins; the ten worst gave back 36% of everything the winners made. The quarter ended −$86. What matters is the gap between the win rate and the break-even rate: about one point below it on gold and a fraction of a point on BTC, decided by a handful of large baskets.

title: One run is one path: the same quarter ends up or down depending on which ticks the loop happens to poll
detail: Gold, 13 Aug–13 Nov 2026, same settings, same ticks: all eight random loop timings ended with the account stopped out, and so did the run with no random delay. BTC: from −$107 to −$25 (median −$47); no random delay −$86. The reason is the pay-off above: whether the bot is inside a basket when a sharp move starts depends on the second it entered, and one such basket outweighs a month of wins. Even at one fixed 0.01-lot unit the result of a gold quarter moved by $939 at the median, and by up to $2,267, with nothing changed but the loop timing. So no single backtest figure, and no single live month, tells you whether a setting is good; only the spread over many runs and many quarters does.

title: The ladder is not a ladder: the last three adds usually go in about two seconds apart, at one price
detail: Each add is released when the RSI of its timeframe is beyond 35 / 65, which is a level, not a new event. When the M15, H1 and H4 RSI are already there, the third, fourth and fifth add fire on consecutive passes of the loop. On gold 64–92% of those adds came within ten seconds of the previous one (median 2 s), $0.30–0.54 away from it; the median spread at its entries is $0.26. So 26 of the 32 units of a full ladder are one clip at one price, not an average-down. Gold baskets that never added made +$1,256 in the quarter; baskets that added lost $3,257; the 26 that reached all six positions account for −$6,160, with an average loss of $1,114 when they lost. BTC shows the same timing (63–93% within ten seconds): +$175 without adds, −$261 with.

title: The only loss exit watches momentum pivots, not price or money, and nothing stands behind it
detail: A losing basket is closed when the M15 RSI / MACD pivot score turns against it (the profit "book" uses the same M15 condition, so it adds nothing: see below). In a steady adverse move that score stays neutral or supportive. The worst gold basket of the quarter was a BUY of 1.60 lots opened on 22 Oct 2026 at 4,069.57: it was held 13.5 hours while price moved $50.40 against its average entry and was closed at −$8,064. 74% of gold's losing baskets were closed within 10% of the worst point they ever showed, 78% had been in profit before, and one basket that ended as a winner had been $2,576 under water on the way. There is no price stop, no time stop and no equity stop, and the stop sent to the broker is not a stop (see the live-code findings).

title: The entry signal says nothing about where price goes next
detail: An entry needs the M15 RSI vote and the M15 MACD vote to agree. Both are measured from the last pivot of their indicator, so both are votes to fade the last extreme: over the fifteen months the MACD vote pointed against its own signal-line trend on 80% of gold's M15 bars (79% for BTC), and 88% of RSI up-votes came after an oversold low. Tested on every closed M15 bar with the live indicator code: after both votes pointed up, gold was higher four bars later 50.8% of the time, against 50.8% for any bar; after both pointed down it was lower 49.9% of the time, against 49.2%. BTC: 51.5% against 50.0%, and 50.8% against 50.0%. That is a coin flip. The wins come from the target being close and the stop being absent, not from the signal knowing direction, which is why the timeframes the signal is read on cannot fix the result.

title: The spread takes a large share of what the winners make
detail: Gold paid $1,701 of spread in the quarter, 4% of the winners' gross profit, on 4 baskets a day; before spread the closed baskets net −$300, after it −$2,001. BTC paid $313 (5% of the winners' gross). The spread was not the same in every quarter (see the hold-out section), and the strategy's result moves with it.

title: The unit auto-step raises the stake after a good run and the next loss is taken at the larger size
detail: The unit is floor(balance / 2,500) + 1, re-derived whenever the account is flat. In the gold quarter: unit 1: 58 baskets, +$1,000 (worst −$1,197); unit 2: 148 baskets, +$1,058 (worst −$1,733); unit 3: 42 baskets, +$2,281 (worst −$2,841); unit 4: 79 baskets, +$6,432 (worst −$2,913); unit 5: 66 baskets, −$12,773 (worst −$8,064). The account stepped up to five units on the way up and gave everything back at unit 5 (−$12,773 in 66 baskets, worst −$8,064). Because the target also scales with the unit while the worst case of a basket has no limit, stepping up multiplies the tail, not the edge.

title: No choice of timeframes makes it pay: settings that look good on one period do not hold on another
detail: 432 combinations of OPEN and FORCE-CLOSE timeframes were run on five quarters (one fixed 0.01-lot unit; "wiped" replays the baskets on a real $2,000 account with the bot's lot sizing). Gold: no setting was profitable in all three analysed quarters without wiping the account. BTC: 31 of 432 settings were profitable in all three analysed quarters without wiping a $2,000 account. On the two hold-out quarters 3% of those were profitable in both and 81% wiped the account in one (mean −$763 a quarter), against 3% and 87% (mean −$1,546) for all settings; rank correlation between the two periods +0.35. No gold setting was profitable in all five quarters without wiping the account. No BTC setting was profitable in all five quarters without wiping the account. Averaged over all five quarters every gold timeframe loses; on BTC only a FORCE-CLOSE on H4 breaks even. Mean net per quarter, gold: FORCE-CLOSE on H4 −$2,823, H1 −$3,676, M30 −$4,021, M15 −$2,177, M5 −$3,404, M1 −$3,899; OPEN containing H4 −$1,331, M5 −$3,382, M30 −$3,472, M15 −$3,596, H1 −$3,805, M1 −$4,257. BTC: FORCE-CLOSE on H4 +$0, H1 −$1,909, M30 −$184, M15 −$404, M5 −$1,242, M1 −$1,605; OPEN containing H4 −$603, H1 −$739, M30 −$751, M15 −$825, M5 −$1,105, M1 −$1,219. The live setting (OPEN H1+M15, FORCE-CLOSE M15) on gold: Aug–Nov 2025 +$765, Nov 2025–Feb 2026 −$12,273, Feb–May 2026 −$3,168, May–Aug 2026 −$9,880, Aug–Nov 2026 +$1,939. Keep in mind that each cell is a single path whose result moves by about $900 a quarter on gold (up to $2,300) and a few hundred dollars on BTC with the loop timing alone.

title: Removing the ladder cuts the worst loss many times over; nothing tested makes the live timeframes reliably profitable
detail: Each what-if changes one rule, or one small package of rules, and leaves the rest live (one fixed unit, three 2026 quarters, single paths). Gold: live settings: −$11,109 over three quarters, worst basket −$5,968, account wiped; no ladder: −$886 over three quarters, worst basket −$212; ladder: adds >= $3 apart: −$16,596 over three quarters, worst basket −$5,403, account wiped; stop: $20 per unit: −$5,620 over three quarters, worst basket −$236, account wiped; no ladder + stop $10: −$603 over three quarters, worst basket −$44; cooldown 30 min: −$7,723 over three quarters, worst basket −$5,543, account wiped; signals on closed bars: −$10,233 over three quarters, worst basket −$2,681, account wiped. BTC: live settings: −$1,149 over three quarters, worst basket −$583; no ladder: −$62 over three quarters, worst basket −$21; ladder: adds >= $300 apart: +$284 over three quarters, worst basket −$271; stop: $20 per unit: −$3,450 over three quarters, worst basket −$123, account wiped; no ladder + stop $10: −$76 over three quarters, worst basket −$11; cooldown 30 min: −$1,765 over three quarters, worst basket −$584; signals on closed bars: −$2,574 over three quarters, worst basket −$523, account wiped. A stop alone turns a rare large loss into frequent medium ones; the ladder is what makes the large loss large. These are directions to test on a demo account, not settings to deploy. Spacing the ladder $3 apart cut gold's worst basket only by about a tenth and BTC's by about half.

title: What does hold up on data it was never fitted to: a with-trend design with a real stop and no ladder (gold)
detail: The improvement search was run on the hedging branch. The two live variants differ only in their profit exit (the $1 target there, the slope book here), and the design that held up closes baskets only at its own stop and target, so with the book switched off it is exactly the same design on this branch. V3-lite: entries only with the H1 trend (H1 MACD signal line), H1 votes with M15 agreement, stop and target 8 H1-volatility units on the whole basket, no ladder, a 12 h pause after a losing basket, book and force-close off. Chosen on Jan 2024 – Jun 2025 and 13 Aug 2025 – 13 Nov 2026, frozen, then run once on Feb – Dec 2023 (three quarters and one two-month block) (every tick, eight loop timings per quarter, a real $2,000 account): gold +$106 per block with no losing run of 32, and +$152 a quarter in 2024 – mid 2025. On BTC no design made money reliably (V3-lite +$7 a quarter in 2023). About 1,200 designs were tried, so the 2023 figure is the honest one. Details: IMPROVEMENT.md on the backtest_hedging branch.

title: Support and resistance, and the other ways to recover a losing position, do not add an edge
detail: Two independent studies of H1, H4 and D1 levels (swing highs and lows, the previous day's and week's high and low, round numbers): price turned at the levels no more often than at placebo prices, and no bounce rule made money after the spread in either period. A few gold breakout and retest rules with the trend were slightly positive in both, but they were found after the fact and did no better than placebo levels in 2025-26. Forty-two position-management mechanisms on the same 32,553 entries (averaging down with a budget, averaging up, break-even and trailing stops, scale-out, hedge lock, zone recovery, stop-and-reverse, martingale): none raised the expectancy. A ladder with equal lots, at most two adds and a hard $60 budget, flat over every market closure, never lost more than $60 (held over closures, up to −$222 on gold), and earned no more than not adding. A hedge lock unlocked on the next signal pays exactly what closing and re-entering pays; a lock that is simply closed later costs one spread more than a stop. Reports: backtest_results/improve/ on the backtest_hedging branch.
